title: Find the Maximum Number of Elements in Subset
pattern: Hash Table Enumeration of Geometric Chains
spaceBreakdown:
- unordered_map<long long,int> cnt: up to n distinct entries → O(n)
- no recursion, no extra arrays
- not counted: input vector
approach: Count occurrences of each value. For each distinct base x>1, walk the chain x, x², x⁴, …: every level except the last needs at least 2 copies (both sides of the peak), the last needs at least 1, giving length 2·levels−1. Handle 1s separately: any odd count of 1s forms a valid subset. Since x^(2^k) exceeds 10⁹ after ≤5 squarings, total work is O(n).
hints:
The pattern is symmetric around its peak - how many copies of each power of x do the two halves force you to have, and what does the peak itself need?
Values are positive and up to 10⁹, so how many times can you square a number ≥ 2 before it leaves the range?
Use a hash map of counts. For nums = [5,4,1,2,2]: starting at x=2, count[2]=2 covers both sides, then count[4]=1 can only be the peak → subset [2,4,2] of length 3.

**All ones** - every element is 1, only an odd count works.
`Input: [1,1,1,1]` → `Expected: 3`
⚠️ Bug: taking all cnt[1]=4 copies → returns 4 (even count can't be a peak-centered pattern).

**Single copy of each value** - no value appears twice, so every chain is just the peak.
`Input: [1,3,2,4]` → `Expected: 1`
⚠️ Bug: requiring cnt[cur] ≥ 2 even at the last level → returns 0.

**Overflow on squaring** - x near 10⁹ squared exceeds 2³¹−1 (10⁹² ≈ 10¹⁸).
`Input: [1000000000, 1000000000]` → `Expected: 1`
⚠️ Bug: computing cur*cur in int → undefined behavior / wrong wraparound value, may return 3.

**Duplicates needed on both sides** - two copies of the base but one of its square.
`Input: [2,2,4]` → `Expected: 3`
⚠️ Bug: stopping the whole chain when cnt[4] < 2 without checking it as a peak → returns 2.

followUps.q: What if nums[i] can be up to 10¹⁸?
followUps.a: Chains shrink to at most 3 levels (x, x², x⁴), so the same enumeration still runs in O(n); just use unsigned 64-bit / __int128 checks before squaring to avoid overflow. Time and space stay O(n).

followUps.q: What if you must return the actual subset, not just its size?
followUps.a: While walking each chain, record the values and their needed multiplicities (2 per inner level, 1 at the peak), keeping the best chain found. Extra space becomes O(log log max) per stored answer, time still O(n).

followUps.q: What if the array is streamed and cannot be stored (O(1) memory)?
followUps.a: You cannot reconstruct counts of arbitrary values in O(1) space exactly; a practical answer is a heavy-hitters / Count-Min sketch to keep candidate small bases, giving an approximate answer in O(n) time and O(1) memory. Exactness is sacrificed unless values are bounded to a small range.
